newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Gold-Miners commit to forward sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Gold-Miners commit to forward sales.

text.p: Despite some notable early close outs of positions, Australia's gold miners are heavily committed to the use of forward selling instruments, industry experts said on Tuesday.

About 59 percent of Australia's gold industry profits in 1996 was derived from profits on forward selling, up from 40 percent in 1995, said Wayne Lonergan, a partner in the Coopers and Lybrand accounting firm.
"An even larger proportion of profits this year will from forward sales," Lonergan told a meeting of investors.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell analyst Wayne Billington said forward selling was limiting the upside for gold.
"Hedging has the impact of lowering the spot price," he said.
A combination of low interest rates, a strengthening Australian dollar and higher gold lease rates now means forward selling is less attractive, Lonergan said.
However, forward selling effectively guarantees a company's "stay in business money," Lonergan added.
"Accordingly, although forward selling is less attractive in profit terms than was previously the case, it continues to offer significant commercial benefits," Lonergan said.
Richard Windsor, a director of gold mining house Australian Resources Ltd, said tailoring the right hedging programme has never been more difficult.
"Things are a lot tougher now," Windsor said.
"Low gold prices, life contangos, volatility in the gold borrowing costs and the strenghthening Australian dollar make it a lot harder for a producer to replace the hedge cover."
Windsor said most Australian miners maintained about 18 months of hedge cover.
"But what do you do to replace that when you've picked the point where you start to sell," Windsor said.
One option may be to sell more options to enhance the forward sales price, or extend further out flat forward positions, he said.
"There's a lot of things we can do, but it obviously is going to be a lot harder than it was in the past," Windsor said.
The situation for Australia's legion of junior mining houses can be particularly trying due to varying views on forward selling, Windsor said.
"Their bankers insist on it but then they sometimes have to put up with the counter view from some of the fund managers who say 'don't forward sell, we don't like it'," Windsor said.
Lonergan estimates Australia's 20 largest gold companies held a total hedge position of 21.2 million ounces in 1996, up from 17.7 million ounces in 1995.
